key_insight: The paper introduces a simple DDIM-style sampler, pDDIM, that makes diffusion-based posterior sampling for linear inverse problems both more practical and more theoretically grounded. It achieves strong reconstruction performance with only lightweight coordinate-wise changes to the standard DDIM update.
problem_solved: It addresses the challenge of solving linear inverse problems using diffusion priors when existing posterior samplers are either computationally expensive or lack provable guarantees.
method: Starts from a standard DDIM sampler and adds lightweight coordinate-wise modifications tailored to inverse problems.
Explicitly incorporates the linear measurement operator and observed data into each denoising step.
Aims to preserve the efficiency of DDIM while enabling provable posterior sampling behavior.
impact: For practitioners, this offers a faster and simpler way to use diffusion models for tasks like reconstruction, denoising, and restoration under measurement constraints. The added theoretical guarantees make the method more trustworthy for real-world deployment.

paper_title: Provable diffusion-based posterior sampling for linear inverse problems via DDIM
paper_authors: Yuchen Jiao, Na Li, Changxiao Cai, Yuxin Chen, Gen Li
